transcript.text:
Thank you all for these critical flags. Let me summarize the four issues we need to resolve before Monday's signing and my proposed approach for each.

First, Sofia — your benchmark showing the market ceiling at 2.25% is significant. A 3% royalty would be 75 basis points above our validated ceiling. I recommend we go back to Northlake and propose reducing the running royalty to 2.25%, citing the comparable license data.

Second, Daniel — the missing inventor assignment for the continuation application is a title defect we cannot ignore. I recommend we make execution of the missing assignment a condition precedent in the license, or at minimum obtain it before Monday. We cannot close with a gap in the chain of title.

Third, Nora — the ECCN 3A001 classification means we need export-control provisions added to the draft. I recommend we insert clauses prohibiting transfers to military end users and requiring annual end-use screening certifications, as you described.

Fourth, Martin — the prior grant to the University Research Consortium for academic research and teaching uses means our exclusive license needs a carveout. Otherwise we're representing exclusivity we don't actually have. I recommend we add a carveout clause for those existing uses before signing.

Given all four issues, I do not believe we can sign on Monday as scheduled unless we either resolve all four items by then or structure the license to include appropriate conditions, carveouts, and revised terms. I'd like each of you to get me your detailed findings in writing by end of day so I can revise the approval package and the license draft. Does anyone see a path to resolving any of these faster, or do we need to push the signing date?

Excellent work, all four of you. Let me synthesize where we stand and what I'll do tonight.

Daniel, I agree with your condition-precedent recommendation. We should not delay signing for the entire platform over one continuation application, but we also cannot close the title gap. I'll structure it so the license vests rights in the continuation application only upon execution and recording of the missing assignment, with Northlake obligated to procure it. This protects the company and keeps Monday feasible for the other applications.

Nora, please include the broader export-law compliance language alongside the military end-user prohibition and annual screening certification. I want the provisions to be comprehensive enough that we're not creating obligations we can't meet, as you noted.

Martin, I agree the carveout should be framed as a reservation of rights, not a permitted-use concession. I'll make sure the business team understands that our exclusivity does not extend to academic research and teaching uses already granted to the consortium. That's an expectations-management issue I'll address in the approval package.

Sofia, your point about the royalty being the critical path is well taken. Here's my decision: I will prepare a revised license draft tonight incorporating all three drafting fixes — Daniel's condition precedent, Nora's export provisions, and Martin's carveout. In parallel, I'll open a conversation with Northlake's counsel today to propose the 2.25% royalty rate, backed by Sofia's benchmark data. If Northlake agrees in principle by Friday, we can either incorporate the reduced rate directly or use a side letter, and proceed with signing on Monday. If Northlake pushes back and we cannot reach agreement on the rate, I will recommend we push the signing date rather than execute at 3%.

So the plan is: all written findings to me by end of day today; I revise the draft and approval package tonight; I contact Northlake on the royalty tomorrow morning; we assess by Friday whether Monday signing is viable. Does anyone see any issue with that approach?
